name: Extragonadal Germinoma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Germ Cell Tumors

criteria.description: Histological confirmation of germinoma with typical large cells and lymphocytic infiltrate
Tumor located outside gonads, commonly in mediastinum, pineal gland, or retroperitoneum
Normal or mildly elevated serum alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) and beta-human chorionic gonadotropin (β-hCG)
Radiologic evidence of a well-defined mass with homogeneous enhancement on CT or MRI

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of germinoma in an extragonadal site with compatible imaging findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Serum tumor markers help exclude non-germinomatous germ cell tumors

pathognomonic.notes: Common in pineal or suprasellar germinomas

pathognomonic.symptomName: Mediastinal mass causing superior vena cava syndrome
searchTerms: mediastinal mass blocking superior vena cava
tumor causing upper body vein congestion

common.symptomName: Headache due to increased intracranial pressure
searchTerms: head pain from increased intracranial pressure

common.notes: Especially with pineal or suprasellar involvement

searchTerms: persistent cough and shortness of breath

occasional.notes: Due to β-hCG secretion in some cases

searchTerms: lower back pain from tumor behind abdomen
backache due to deep abdominal mass
brain inflammation causing memory and mood changes
blood clot in superior vena cava
superior vena cava blockage by clot

laboratory: Normal or mildly elevated serum AFP and β-hCG
Elevated lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) in some cases
imaging: Well-circumscribed homogeneous mass on CT or MRI
Mass effect on adjacent structures depending on location
genetic: No consistent germline mutations; somatic KIT mutations reported in some tumors
other: Histopathology showing large cells with clear cytoplasm and lymphocytic infiltrate
Immunohistochemistry positive for placental alkaline phosphatase (PLAP) and c-KIT (CD117)

distinguishingFeatures: Elevated LDH and systemic B symptoms
Absence of germ cell tumor markers

redFlags: Rapidly enlarging mediastinal mass causing airway obstruction
Signs of increased intracranial pressure with neurological deterioration
Markedly elevated AFP or β-hCG suggesting non-germinomatous tumor
references: Murray MJ, et al. Extragonadal Germ Cell Tumors: Diagnosis and Management. Oncologist. 2020.
WHO Classification of Tumours Editorial Board. WHO Classification of Tumours: Soft Tissue and Bone Tumours. 5th ed. 2020.
